forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVE-NO. Iran did not publicly commit to resuming ceasefire negotiations before EOD 2026-09-06. Iran executed ballistic missile strikes against US bases on September 1-2 (IRGC struck Bahrain, Jordan, Iraq following US CENTCOM strikes on IRGC targets). FM Araghchi made no qualifying statement; SNSC issued no readiness-for-talks declaration. No TIER1 source reported any Iranian official committing to mediated negotiations. The ambiguity rule applies: Araghchi's formulations in this period were conditional preconditions not publicly accepted by the US, resolving AMBIGUOUS-NO. Resolution: NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Araghchi or SNSC public statement committing to talks
Oman or Qatar mediator readout citing named Iranian acceptance

forecasts.question: Will a confirmed Iran-US indirect negotiating session (mediated by a named third party, with senior officials from both sides participating, however formatted) occur before EOD 2026-09-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE (-6pp; DA floor 0.09 accepted). The September 11 US CENTCOM strikes on Hormuzgan air defense and coastal surveillance installations, followed within hours by IRGC ballistic missile salvos on Prince Hassan Airbase (Jordan), a Bahrain logistics facility, and Camp Titin, constitute the heaviest bilateral exchange in over a month. No TIER1 or mediator source reported a convened session or scheduled meeting date in the Sep 3-12 window. The horizon closes September 17 — five days from today — and the bilateral halt precondition (indicator 3) is CONTRADICTED by the Sep 11-12 exchange. DA floor accepted: p=0.09 rather than 0.08, reflecting that Oman's facilitation channel has historically remained open even during peak exchanges. Two independent TIER1 sources confirming a session would be required to resolve YES; none exist today.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a formally convened indirect negotiating session — conducted in any format (in-room with mediator, video-call, sequential room via mediator) — between named US and Iranian senior officials/envoys, hosted by a named mediating country or organization (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar/Switzerland), between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official mediator readout from the mediating country's foreign ministry.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Message relay through intermediaries without a formally convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump assertions of 'semi-negotiating' without Iranian or mediator confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If a mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar) claims a session occurred but Iran publicly denies it, resolve AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO pending a second independent TIER1 confirmation.

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reach >=30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average) before EOD 2026-10-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE (-11pp; DA range 0.10-0.11, setting 0.11). AIS-tracking as of September 9-10 shows Hormuz at a 10-day rolling average of 14 commercial vessels per day — far below the 30/day threshold. On September 9, only 7 vessels transited; no LNG tankers recorded. More critically, the IRGC was caught deploying additional sea mines on approximately September 10-11, directly triggering US CENTCOM strikes on Hormuzgan Province on September 11 (NBC News, CENTCOM; Trump Truth Social Sep 11). The sustained-halt indicator is now CONTRADICTED. Reaching 30/day within 21 days requires a complete halt in Iranian mine deployment, CENTCOM MCM clearance of new fields, and rapid insurer re-entry — an implausible sequence in the current bilateral exchange environment. Sources: Straits.live Sep 9-10; Al Jazeera Sep 3 Hormuz data analysis; RFE/RL Sep 10 traffic report.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any of the named AIS-based ship-tracking sources (MarineTraffic, Straits.live, Lloyd's List Intelligence, Kpler, IMF PortWatch) records >=30 commercial transits/day as a 7-day rolling average at any point between 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-03. Commercial transit means civilian cargo/tanker passage; naval escort and warship movements excluded.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Named AIS-based tracker (see resolution_criteria) + one TIER1 or OSINT confirmation (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval escort vessels and warships do not count toward commercial transit. Oil tankers transiting under active naval escort without separate commercial registration are excluded. If named AIS trackers diverge by >20% on the same date, flag AMBIGUOUS and hold resolution until trackers converge or a named mediator confirms traffic counts.

forecasts.question: Will Likud win the most Knesset seats (seat plurality) in the October 27, 2026 Israeli election?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE (+3pp). An i24NEWS/Direct Polls survey published approximately September 6 put Likud at 27 mandates versus Yashar at 22 — the first poll in several weeks placing Likud at >=25 seats. A concurrent KAN News poll reversed the order: Yashar 24, Likud 21. The spread between the two polls (6-seat divergence) precludes a trend call. Netanyahu confirmed he will stand as Likud leader. DA hygiene correction applied: first indicator wording fixed from '>= 23 seats ahead of Yashar' (unreachable 23-seat gap) to '>=23 mandates in own seat count.' forecasts.question: Will Iran (IRGC or Iranian military) launch at least one ballistic or cruise missile strike against a US military installation in the Middle East, beyond and after the September 11-12 exchange, before EOD 2026-09-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 72h forecast (DA reframe applied: Sep 11-12 exchange explicitly excluded per critical audit finding). On September 11-12, the IRGC executed its confirmed salvo against Prince Hassan Airbase (Jordan), a US logistics facility in Bahrain, and Camp Titin (Jordan/Aqaba). This forecast asks whether a FURTHER wave follows, not whether the Sep 11-12 exchange occurred. Pattern: IRGC follow-on waves within 48-72h observed in approximately 7 of 9 prior comparable exchange cycles since March 2026 (Stars and Stripes Aug 27, CENTCOM after-action log). However, IRGC Brigadier General Naini's Sep 12 framing — 'enhanced deterrence postures' rather than a specific strike warning — and the deliberate targeting of infrastructure rather than personnel centers argues for a calibrated pause at approximately 45%. DA partial-accept: initial estimate 0.60 reduced to 0.55 for the deliberate-calibration discount.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if CENTCOM or a TIER1 source (Reuters/AP/AFP/BBC) confirms at least one IRGC or Iranian military ballistic or cruise missile detonation at or near a US military installation in the Middle East, OCCURRING AFTER the September 11-12 exchange (i.e., originating or impacting after 06:00 UTC September 12, 2026), before EOD September 15, 2026. The September 11 night strikes and their immediate IRGC response salvo (all confirmed before 06:00 UTC September 12) do NOT count toward this forecast.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM official statement identifying a new, separate strike incident from the Sep 11-12 exchange, OR two independent TIER1 outlets reporting the same new incident.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Iranian drone strikes fully intercepted before reaching US facilities = NO unless CENTCOM confirms structural damage at or near a facility from a Sep 12-15 originated attack. Non-ballistic fire from Iran-linked proxies (mortar, RPG, small-UAS) = NO unless IRGC officially claims the specific action. Proxy-fired ballistic missiles without IRGC claim of responsibility = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. The Sep 11-12 IRGC salvo is explicitly excluded from YES resolution.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVE-NO. The Knesset dissolved July 17, 2026 at the natural end of its four-year term (first completion of a full parliamentary term since 1988; Al Jazeera, Times of Israel Jul 17). The coalition maintained a one-seat majority (61/120) through the dissolution; no Knesset roll-call vote confirmed loss of majority before that date. Resolution criteria: 'NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.' The mandatory election date is October 27, 2026; the coalition survived to that point with 61+ seats intact through the July natural dissolution. No further path to YES exists. Resolution: NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran observe a mutual halt in offensive strikes lasting >=48 consecutive hours before EOD 2026-09-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 10-day forecast (source rule corrected per DA audit; IRNA/Tasnim silence removed as evidence of inaction). As of September 12, US-Iran bilateral exchange is at highest kinetic tempo in over a month: US CENTCOM struck Hormuzgan Sep 11; IRGC responded with ballistic missiles on three US facilities the same night. No mediator-confirmed halt or announced operational pause exists. Prior exchange cycles show spontaneous 48-72h pauses have occurred (before the April 8 ceasefire; after August 14 wave), requiring either a political signal from one side or a mediator readout to hold. Neither condition is present today. P=0.12 reflects low-but-nonzero base rate of an operational pause within 10 days of a major exchange.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, between 2026-09-12 and 2026-09-22, there is a documented period of >=48 consecutive hours during which neither CENTCOM nor IRGC conducts offensive strikes against the other's military assets or territory, confirmed by CENTCOM operational reports AND independent OSINT sources (ADS-B Exchange, Planet Labs commercially available imagery, or named tracking services such as C4ISRNET/The War Zone) showing no kinetic events attributed to IRGC in the same 48h window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM daily operational reports (no-strike entries for the 48h period) PLUS at least one of: a named third-party mediator's (Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) readout affirming restraint by both sides, OR OSINT flight/satellite monitoring (ADS-B Exchange, Planet Labs publicly released imagery) showing no IRGC-attributed kinetic events for the 48h window. IRNA or Tasnim silence alone is NOT sufficient as evidence of Iranian inaction.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: US or allied air defense intercepts of incoming Iranian missiles do not count as offensive action by the US. Iranian proxy/militia strikes (Houthi, PMF, Hezbollah) without direct IRGC ballistic/cruise missile involvement = NO unless IRGC officially claims the specific action. A unilateral US halt without confirmed Iranian parallel halt = NO. CENTCOM 'defensive preemptive' strikes against IRGC launcher positions — which CENTCOM may frame as force-protection — are counted as offensive action for purposes of this forecast.

indicators.expected_effect: +35pp toward YES if combined with confirmed Iranian parallel pause

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran reach any form of bilateral de-escalation agreement (written or oral, publicly announced, mediated) before EOD 2026-11-30?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 79-day forecast. Pezeshkian's standing offer to reciprocate a US return to the June 17 MOU had not been formally withdrawn as of September 8 (Al Jazeera). The June MOU lapsed August 17; Trump ordered US envoys to halt contacts August 18. Two prior cycles demonstrate rapid bilateral agreements: April 8 ceasefire after February-March exchange; June 17 MOU after May exchange. September 11-12 exchange follows a longer pattern of MOU failure and renewed kinetics; political appetite in Washington for a third framework is unconfirmed. Base rate of a third agreement by November 30: 20%, reflecting the historical precedent for rapid diplomatic pivots alongside deepened mutual mistrust.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-11-30, a public announcement from both US and Iranian official sources confirms agreement on any bilateral framework including at minimum: (a) a halt or reduction in direct US-Iran offensive strikes, AND (b) a named mediator or implementation mechanism. A unilateral US or Iranian ceasefire declaration not acknowledged by the other party = NO.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP PLUS one Iranian state media source (IRNA/Tasnim) both confirming the agreement, OR a named mediator country's foreign ministry readout confirming both parties have accepted the framework.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A framework covering only one track (only Hormuz transit, only nuclear talks) without addressing direct US-Iran military strikes = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Informal working arrangements not publicly confirmed = NO. A temporary operational pause without a named agreement = NO.
